root_cause_label: ALS Observed-Entry Validation Illusion: agent validates only on seen entries and mistakes high observed-fit for full reconstruction quality, while chosen ALS method diverges from benchmark nuclear-norm approach
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent validates its ALS-based matrix completion solely on the 4000 observed entries (RMSE ~0.01, correlation ~0.9999) and treats this as sufficient quality evidence, never checking reconstruction quality on unobserved entries, which is what the hidden evaluation measures.
t_err_evidence: Step 9: agent writes complete.py committing to ALS with rank=5 using hardcoded n_rows=n_cols=200 (unverified from step 7 which produced no output) and buggy boolean indexing (vals[mask[i, cols_i]]), making the first decisive mistake in both algorithmic choice (ALS vs. benchmark nuclear-norm) and implementation.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16: final_complete.py runs successfully and writes all 20 solution_i.txt files using the ALS method with only observed-entry validation. At this point all output files are committed to disk and the agent moves to cleanup/verification, locking in the failure.
trigger_explanation: At step 9 the agent assumes the matrix is 200x200 (the step 7 Python stats query produced no output but was treated as confirmed) and at step 14 the agent incorrectly treats excellent observed-entry fit (RMSE=0.011, correlation=0.9999) as proof that the reconstruction is correct, never realizing the hidden evaluation measures similarity to the true underlying matrix across all entries including unobserved ones.
forewarning_evidence: Step 7: Python command to compute row/column range statistics and value mean/std produced '(command executed successfully with no output)'. Agent proceeded at step 8 as if the statistics were confirmed, asserting specific values (rows/cols 0-199, mean ~0.04, std ~0.59) that were never actually printed.
